completed_acceptance_criteria: AC1 all 8 nightly file-ingestion failures pass, none skipped (11 pass / 1 pre-existing skip / 0 fail)

AC2 root cause identified as a PRODUCT defect, not test infrastructure: caseDocumentSchema validated tenantId/createdBy/updatedBy/principalId/grantedBy/signedBy/relatedCaseId/relatedContactId/id/parentVersionId as z.uuid() while Prisma issues @default(cuid()) ids for Tenant and User

AC3 blast radius confirmed reachable: documents.upload (upload.router.ts:125) and email-inbound (email-inbound.router.ts:67) pass ctx.user.tenantId / ctx.user.userId straight into ingestFile, so every cuid-issued tenant got a 500 on document upload

AC4 fix is idiomatic and layering-correct: entityIdSchema = union(uuid, cuid) defined in domain, mirroring idSchema in @intelliflow/validators (which cannot be imported here because validators depends on domain, not vice versa)
AC5 CaseDocument.mimeType / .sizeBytes getters added — fields were persisted and schema-validated but read back undefined from the aggregate
AC6 no regression: 7127 domain/application/adapters tests pass; caseDocumentSchema was the only domain schema validating tenantId as a UUID
test_defects_corrected: tenant-1 / tenant-2 / user-123 matched no id format AND had no tenants row to satisfy case_documents_tenant_id_fkey; replaced with cuid-shaped ids plus real tenant rows upserted in beforeAll and cascade-deleted in afterAll

failure-event assertions used the class name 'DocumentIngestionFailedEvent' instead of the domain eventType 'document.ingestion_failed' (2 sites); the success-path assertion already used the correct dotted form, confirming drift

the antivirus spec uploaded application/x-msdownload, which validateFile() rejects before the scanner runs, so it asserted 'virus detected' against a MIME-rejection message; now uses an allowed MIME type
events[0].data.documentId read a property DomainEvent does not expose; now events[0].toPayload().documentId
the infected-file spec now uses a dedicated uploader so its 'document was NOT saved' assertion stays meaningful once the earlier specs genuinely persist documents

notes: ENG-OPS-003 governance Gap #9 (attestation-tracked, NOT a Sprint_plan.csv row — like Gaps #1/#2/#5/#6/#7/#12/#13/#14; no CSV flip). PR #646 fixed the Prisma 7 driver-adapter constructor in this suite, which unmasked 8 real failures on the 2026-07-25 nightly (run 30160486859, integration-tests FAIL at 0cba18d9). Those 8 were NOT test-infrastructure noise: seven reported only 'expected false to be true' because the spec discarded result.error, hiding the actual cause. Reproducing the pipeline locally against Postgres :5433 with a stub storage adapter surfaced it immediately — CaseDocument.create() threw a Zod 'Invalid UUID' on tenantId, because caseDocumentSchema demanded UUIDs for identity fields that Prisma issues as cuids. Confirmed with a real tenant row (cmqjf6orv0000vwp57bsecutg, 'Talysson Oliveira's Organization'), so document upload was broken in production for every tenant created through normal onboarding, not just for the test's synthetic ids. packages/validators/src/common.ts already documents this exact hazard and ships idSchema = union(uuid, cuid); caseDocumentSchema simply never adopted it. Fix redefines that union locally as entityIdSchema because the dependency runs validators -> domain. A second latent product gap surfaced once ingestion succeeded: CaseDocument exposed no mimeType/sizeBytes getters, so both read undefined off the aggregate despite being persisted and validated; getters added. The remaining four corrections are genuine test-fixture and contract drift, enumerated in evidence_summary.test_defects_corrected. Static reading of the specs pointed at a foreign-key violation; that hypothesis was wrong and only running the pipeline disproved it — the FK is real but the domain schema rejected the input before any SQL was issued. No pre-ship bypass, no --no-verify, no destructive git. All DB work under Node 22 (host default node v25 hangs pg writes). A prod-Supabase .env copied into the worktree during setup was removed before any test ran, because Vitest auto-loads .env and it would have pointed writes at production.
